services.name: Player_ApplyTerrainResponse
services.behavior: Consumes TERRAIN_QUERY_STATE_A and the terrain stop/response flags, applies the player Y correction and camera threshold, refreshes the vertical-band animation when permitted, or cancels velocity and response state; publishes PLAYER_TRANSITION_GATE for the next frame.

services.name: Player_SelectVerticalBandAnimationOnOddFrame
services.behavior: Runs only on odd FRAME_PHASE_COUNTER phases and, when PLAYER_INTERACTION_ANIMATION_GATE is clear, maps PLAYER_WORLD_Y>>2 & 0xF to a player animation root, sets PLAYER_FACING_X_FLIP for bands above 7, and clears PLAYER_ANIMATION_TIMER.

services.name: Player_SelectVerticalBandAnimation
services.behavior: Performs the same vertical-band animation-root selection without the odd-frame phase gate.

data.name: PLAYER_VERTICAL_ANIMATION_TABLE
data.behavior: Sixteen longword pointers to player animation streams; entries are selected by the four-bit vertical band derived from PLAYER_WORLD_Y.

evidence.frame_path: Game_FrameUpdateLoop calls the terrain/motion region before MovementVM and actor collision; 0x001A986E calls the gated selector from its correction branches and the ungated selector when vertical motion is canceled.
evidence.selection_contract: The 0x001A9986 instruction sequence references ROM 0x00121828, computes (PLAYER_WORLD_Y >> 2) & 0x0F, writes PLAYER_ANIMATION_PC and PLAYER_ANIMATION_TIMER, and sets the facing flip for indices 8..15.
evidence.response_contract: 0x001A986E clears or sets PLAYER_TRANSITION_GATE according to terrain-query, response-active, stop, landing, and interaction conditions; correction branches update PLAYER_Y and camera thresholds before selecting the vertical-band stream.

limitations: The table entries are mechanically confirmed as player animation roots, but their individual motion-state meanings remain a separate naming task.
This is static decompilation; no new runtime trace was required because the data flow and caller contract are explicit.
conclusion: The former anonymous player terrain-response region is now named as one connected path: terrain flags resolve through Player_ApplyTerrainResponse, which selects the appropriate vertical-band animation through the gated or ungated selector and the dedicated sixteen-entry ROM table.
